scope: Move justification for a strategic asset created after a materially balanced exchange, including effects absent after the first move. Position-character and played-mistake labels remain separate.
inputs: Use the exact cached root and independently reached reply boards. Both searches must be at least depth 16, agree within 90 centipawns, and allow legal replay through the evidence. Only the leading move and alternatives within 50 centipawns contribute. Every exchange begins within four plies and settles by six plies, covering the original root piece as captor or victim. At settlement the net material change must be within half a pawn of the start.
arms: The shared-shape arm checks the same original passed pawn or newly open rook file. The used-asset arm requires the original pawn to quietly advance and survive, or a rook to enter or travel along the new file. The linked-use arm additionally requires the same original actor and original victims in the two exchanges. Use previews only for screening and compare all arms against the same baseline.
reference: Manually review the exact asset, its use and the scope of the current report. Do not infer a tactical label from checks or an equal capture sequence. Check repeatability on separate classical games and, when present, a deeper legal reply. If no approach adds verifiable explanations at acceptable precision, report the result without changing the classifier.
